comparisons.peer_summary: Competition for skilled executives and employees in AI and machine learning is intense, and failure to attract, train, and retain key personnel could hinder product development, affected by stock-based compensation value and future restructuring plans.
comparisons.comparison: Both Avago and AMD identify the retention of engineering and technical personnel as critical to business strategy and product development. Avago explicitly cites competition in Silicon Valley and Southeast Asia, as well as immigration laws, as constraints on the talent pool. AMD similarly highlights intense competition for skilled executives and employees in AI and machine learning. Both companies disclose that stock performance and the value of share-based compensation directly impact their ability to attract and retain these key employees; Avago notes that stock underperformance could impair retention efforts, while AMD warns that if stock awards do not appreciate, the ability to motivate and retain executives could be weakened.

sentences.text: Competition for these employees is significant in many areas of the world in which we operate, particularly in Silicon Valley and Southeast Asia where qualified engineers are in high demand.
In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.

If we are not able to continue to attract, train and retain our leadership team and our qualified employees necessary for our business, the progress of our product development programs could be hindered, and we could be materially adversely affected.

If the value of such stock awards does not appreciate as measured by the performance of the price of our common stock, or if our share-based compensation otherwise ceases to be viewed as a valuable benefit, our ability to attract, retain and motivate our executives and employees could be weakened, which could harm our results of operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital Challenges and Workforce Turnover
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces intense competition for technical talent, which is exacerbated by remote work flexibility and immigration policies. High turnover and restructuring efforts, including headcount reductions in 2022 and 2024, along with reduced retention value of share-based awards due to stock price declines, can harm operations and recruitment.
comparisons.comparison: Avago and Intel both face intense competition for technical talent, with both explicitly citing changes in immigration policies as a factor that limits the available pool of qualified engineers and professionals. Avago states that immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers. Intel notes that changes in immigration policies may further limit the pool of available talent. Both companies utilize share-based awards (such as RSUs) to help attract and retain qualified employees. Avago links stock performance to retention success, while Intel notes that they use share-based awards to help attract, retain, and motivate qualified employees, though Intel also uniquely highlights the disruption caused by recent workforce reductions and high turnover in the context of these retention challenges.

sentences.text: In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.
Competitors for technical talent often seek to hire our employees, and the availability of flexible, hybrid, or work-from-home arrangements has both intensified and expanded competition.
In addition, changes in immigration policies may further limit the pool of available talent and impair our ability to recruit and hire technical and professional talent.
To help attract, retain, and motivate qualified employees, we use share-based awards, such as RSUs, and performance-based cash incentive awards.

comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital and Talent Retention Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company must attract and retain highly skilled employees to remain competitive; high attrition, intense competition for talent, and immigration policy changes may increase costs or disrupt operations.
comparisons.comparison: Avago and Micron both report that competition for qualified talent is intense and that immigration policy changes may limit the ability to hire and retain employees. Avago specifies that current or future immigration laws may limit the pool of available talent. Micron similarly states that changes to immigration policies may limit the ability to hire and/or retain talent in specific locations. Both companies emphasize the critical nature of retaining skilled employees to maintain competitiveness and business operations, with Avago noting the importance of equity granting philosophy and Micron noting the risk of business disruptions and increased expenses due to significant attrition.

sentences.text: Competition for these employees is significant in many areas of the world in which we operate, particularly in Silicon Valley and Southeast Asia where qualified engineers are in high demand.
In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.
Hiring, retaining and motivating qualified executives and other skilled talent is critical to our business and competition can be intense.

Additionally, changes to immigration policies in the countries in which we operate, as well as restrictions on travel due to public health crises or other causes, may limit our ability to hire and/or retain talent in, or transfer talent to, specific locations.
Our inability to do so could inhibit our ability to maintain or expand our business operations and may adversely impact our operating results.

comparisons.peer_topic: Executive and Key Employee Retention Risk
comparisons.peer_summary: The business depends on attracting, retaining, and motivating executives and key employees, including a longstanding executive team, to execute its strategy. Risks include competitive labor markets, immigration regulation changes, and the potential decrease in the retentive value of stock-based compensation during periods of stock price volatility.
comparisons.comparison: Avago and NVIDIA both identify the need to attract, retain, and motivate executives and key employees as critical to executing business strategy. Both companies explicitly cite changes in immigration and work permit regulations as factors that could impair their ability to attract and retain qualified employees. Furthermore, both companies disclose risks related to the value of stock-based compensation; Avago notes that stock underperformance could impair retention efforts, while NVIDIA highlights that in times of stock price volatility, the retentive value of stock-based compensation may decrease, necessitating increased cash and stock-based compensation costs.

sentences.text: If we are unable to attract and retain qualified personnel, especially our engineering and technical personnel, we may not be able to execute our business strategy effectively.
In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.
If we are unable to continue our current equity granting philosophy or our stock underperforms, this could impair our efforts to attract and retain necessary personnel.
If we are unable to attract, retain and motivate our executives and key employees, our business may be harmed.
Changes in immigration and work permit regulations or in their administration or interpretation could impair our ability to attract and retain qualified employees.

Competition for personnel results in increased costs in the form of cash and stock-based compensation, and in times of stock price volatility, as we have experienced in the past and may experience in the future, the retentive value of our stock-based compensation may decrease.

comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital Retention and Recruitment Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces intense competition for specialized engineering talent and key management, exacerbated by remote work options, larger competitors with superior compensation or benefits, and restrictive immigration laws for foreign national graduates.
comparisons.comparison: Avago and Qualcomm both emphasize that their future success depends on attracting and retaining specialized engineering and technical personnel, noting that these skills are in high demand and highly competitive. Both companies explicitly cite immigration laws as a barrier that makes it more difficult to recruit and retain qualified talent. Avago mentions that immigration laws may limit the pool of available talent, particularly in Silicon Valley and Southeast Asia. Qualcomm states that existing immigration laws make it more difficult to recruit and retain highly skilled foreign national graduates, making the pool of available talent even smaller.

sentences.text: Competition for these employees is significant in many areas of the world in which we operate, particularly in Silicon Valley and Southeast Asia where qualified engineers are in high demand.
In addition, current or future immigration laws may make it more difficult to hire or retain qualified engineers, further limiting the pool of available talent.

Our future success depends upon the continued service of our executive officers and other key management and technical personnel, and on our ability to continue to identify, attract, retain and motivate them.

In addition, in order to extend our business into certain new and expanded product areas and industries and applications beyond mobile handsets, we need to attract, retain and motivate engineering and other technical personnel with specialized skills in these areas, and these skills are in high demand among our competitors.

Further, existing immigration laws make it more difficult for us to recruit and retain highly skilled foreign national graduates of universities in the United States, making the pool of available talent even smaller.
